clue.text: Fashion models rarely showing up

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of the next word are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Catwalk models are seldom seen turning up to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up' is a link here: MODELS rearranged gives the answer. Note that MODELS read backwards is SLEDOM, so it is not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean not often, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: English female sheep's cheese

parts.note: a dam is the female parent of an animal such as a sheep

explanation.surface: A cheese made in England from ewes' milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a well-known Dutch cheese, so cheese names its general category.

clue.text: French artist draws Bolt, the playwright

parts.note: Jacques-Louis David was a French neoclassical painter
to bolt is to run off fast, which is to hare

explanation.surface: A French painter sketches the sprinter Usain Bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt looks like the Jamaican sprinter, but it is the verb meaning to rush off, as in 'hare away'. 'draws' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir David Hare is a celebrated English dramatist, so he fits as an example of a playwright.

clue.text: People take time to get on

parts.note: man in the sense of humankind means people collectively
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Folk need time to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on can mean to cope or get by, which is a sense of manage.

clue.text: Glenn, for example, is fast bowler

parts.note: the contracted form of is, as in it's, gives S
in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Glenn, say, bowls quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth. The surface suggests the Australian fast bowler Glenn McGrath, adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronaut John Glenn is an example of someone who travelled into space.

clue.text: Supporting new and old type of school

parts.note: secondary can mean supporting or subordinate, as in a secondary role
modern means new or up to date

explanation.surface: Backing both new and old styles of school.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern was a type of British state school for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam, largely phased out from the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: This school category belonged to the old British tripartite system and is now mostly gone, so it is fairly called an old type.

clue.text: Saw soldiers involved in terrible mishap

indicators.note: being involved in something puts the soldiers inside the other piece
terrible signals that the letters of mishap are thrown into disorder

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops caught up in a dreadful accident were seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning a proverb. 'terrible' rearranges MISHAP as APHISM, and 'involved in' puts the soldiers inside it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, and an aphorism is a pithy maxim, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: German artist in modern style

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A German painter working in a modern manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Dada and Surrealist painter, so he is an example of a German artist.

clue.text: Article's broken down and analysed

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
atomised means reduced to tiny particles, that is broken down

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece has been taken apart and examined.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Article's' is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: To anatomise is to dissect or examine in detail, so the past form is a synonym of analysed.

clue.text: Energetic and endlessly valiant in struggle, wearing George Cross

indicators.note: the George Cross wears, or encloses, the other letters

parts.note: GC is the abbreviation for the George Cross, a British gallantry medal

indicators.note: letters in a struggle are tossed around, so they are rearranged
without its end, the word valiant loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A gallant fighter keeps going, decorated with a George Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts off the final letter to leave VALIAN, which 'in struggle' turns into ALVANI; 'wearing' puts the medal letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanic means sudden and stimulating, as if by an electric shock, so it is a synonym of energetic.

clue.text: Husband's terribly mean about new tennis star

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the new piece
terribly tells us the letters of mean are jumbled

explanation.surface: A husband is being awfully nasty about a new tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns MEAN into EMAN, and 'about' puts N inside it to give ENMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Henman was Britain's leading men's tennis player around 2000, so he is an example of a tennis star.

clue.text: Decline of French stage

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a generation is a stage in a line of descent

explanation.surface: France's fall from grace on the world stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Degeneration is a falling-off in quality, so it is a synonym of decline as a noun.

clue.text: Pictures of girls from Derby, perhaps, and Dundee?

parts.note: Derby is an English cheese, so perhaps marks it as one example
Dundee cake is a Scottish fruit cake

explanation.surface: Photographs of young women from the cities of Derby and Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby and Dundee read as cities but are a cheese and a cake. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is slang for photographs of attractive women posing glamorously.

clue.text: Branch of Islam found in Bangladeshi areas

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Muslim branch that is present in parts of Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Shia Islam is one of the two main branches of the faith, alongside Sunni.

clue.text: He kills when soldiers do bad things

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
SAS is the Special Air Service regiment of the British army
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: A killer strikes while troops misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially of a prominent person, so 'he kills' describes one.

clue.text: Draw old friend

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Sketch a longtime pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching; it is the noun meaning a tied game, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate in chess is a position that results in a draw, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bags containing a couple of black snakes

indicators.note: a couple of letters from the start means the first two of the next word

parts.note: adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Sacks holding two black serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is a link word here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladder is a bag-like organ or inflatable sac, so bags is a plural synonym.

clue.text: Girl finding house at last in LA hills

indicators.note: in places the final letter of house inside the other piece

parts.note: Beverly Hills is a famous district of Los Angeles

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of the word house

explanation.surface: A young woman finally finds a home in the hills of Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverley is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Top contestants' top shots

definitions.meaning: experts or champions in a field are its finest players
in tennis an unreturned serve is the best kind of shot

explanation.surface: The leading competitors' best strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is both a highly skilled performer and an unreturnable serve in tennis.

clue.text: Boys get drum

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name, so two boys can each be Tom
Tom is a boy's name, so two boys can each be Tom

explanation.surface: Lads acquire a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a tall drum beaten with the hands, so it is a type of drum.

clue.text: The Supreme One

parts.note: a being that is supreme comes after nobody, so it ranks behind no-one at all

explanation.definitionFit: Being outranked by nobody means being the best, which is what supreme describes.

clue.text: About to prepare for attack

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
to set is to prepare, as in setting a table

explanation.surface: Ready to get set for an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as a phrase meaning ready to, but the two words split between separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning of an attack or assault, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Evidence one's not in the south of France

indicators.note: one is not in the evidence, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an alibi is evidence that someone was elsewhere
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Proof that someone was not in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an alibi about one person's whereabouts; the definition is a place found in that region.
explanation.definitionFit: Albi is a cathedral city in the Tarn department of southern France, so the phrase locates it.

clue.text: Girl setting off sails east

indicators.note: setting off a mixture disturbs it, so the letters of sails are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman sets off as the sails are pointed east.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is a Scottish and northern word for a girl.

clue.text: Putting end to disorder in estates shows guts

indicators.note: in places the final letter of disorder inside the other piece

parts.note: an entail is an estate settled on a fixed line of heirs, so entails are estates

indicators.note: end to means take the last letter of the word disorder

explanation.surface: Ending the disorder on the estates shows real guts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage; it means intestines. 'Putting' and 'shows' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the internal organs, especially the intestines, so guts is a synonym.

clue.text: Plane is not about to ditch

annotationWithheld.why: Plane is not about to ditch (8): JET + T(IS)ON needs 'about' both to reverse NOT and to put IS inside it; one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Plane is not about to ditch

clue.text: Fancy Emily Knight? You've a bit of a nerve!

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or decorated, so the letters of Emily are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Fancy that, Emily the knight, you've got some cheek!
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nerve' looks like a remark about cheek; it is literal, the sheath around nerve fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: Myelin is the fatty insulating sheath around many nerve fibres, so it is literally part of a nerve.
